title: Our al-Aqsa and our captives
summary: Editorial juxtaposing two cases of prisoner treatment. It opens by noting a recently passed Israeli parliamentary measure providing for the execution of Palestinian prisoners, framed as occurring decades after the seizure of Palestine, then pivots to its main subject: the treatment and execution of Sunni prisoners in Iraqi prisons run by Iran-aligned Shia authorities, which it labels the 'Rafidi resistance'. The editorial draws an explicit equivalence between Israel and the Iranian-led Shia axis as enemies of Sunnis, arguing that the loud attention given to al-Aqsa and Palestinian captives stands in contrast to silence over Sunni prisoners in Iraq. It attacks human rights bodies and the legal and parliamentary apparatus as providing cover, and frames the nationalist and resistance framing of the Palestinian cause as a distraction from sectarian persecution. The piece advances IS's characteristic line against the Iran-led resistance axis while folding the Palestinian and prisoner themes into a sectarian narrative.
keyClaims: An Israeli parliamentary measure providing for the execution of Palestinian prisoners is paralleled by the execution of Sunni prisoners in Iraqi prisons run by Iran-aligned Shia authorities.
Israel and the Iranian-led Shia axis are equivalent enemies of Sunnis.
Attention to al-Aqsa and Palestinian captives is selective and ignores Sunni prisoners held by the Iraqi state.
Human rights bodies and legal and parliamentary processes provide cover for the persecution of Sunnis.
The nationalist and resistance framing of the Palestinian cause distracts from sectarian persecution.
significanceAssessment: Advances IS's long-standing strategy of attacking the Iran-led resistance axis and equating it with Israel, while redirecting the Palestinian and al-Aqsa cause toward its own sectarian narrative about Sunni prisoners. Signals continued hostility to both Israel and the Iran-aligned Shia camp, and to mainstream pro-Palestinian mobilisation. The prisoner theme reinforces in-group grievance and delegitimises rivals.
notes: Issue number and Hijri date (14 Shawwal 1447) read from masthead and cross-checked against the consecutive Shawwal issues 542 and 543; converted to Gregorian 2 April 2026. 'Rafidi resistance' is the source's label for Iran-aligned Iraqi Shia militias, rendered neutrally here. Editorial page only.
